enonce_markdown: Which of the following words is stressed on the **second** syllable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

In English, most two-syllable nouns are stressed on the first syllable, but many verbs and words with a prefix such as *be-* are stressed on the second.

### Solution

DOC-tor, FAR-mer and MAR-ket are all stressed on the first syllable. *Begin* is stressed on the second: be-GIN. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: The word *record* has the stress on the first syllable when it is a noun (REcord) and on the second when it is a verb (reCORD). In which sentence is *record* stressed on the **second** syllable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Two-syllable words spelt alike often shift stress: noun = first syllable, verb = second syllable.

### Solution

In (a), (c) and (d), *record* is a noun (REcord). Only in (b) is it a verb ("to record"), so it is said reCORD. **Answer: b.**

choix.texte: I want to record the lesson.
He keeps a record of his sales.

enonce_markdown: Which of the following words is stressed on its **third** syllable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Count the syllables, then say the word aloud and mark the strongest one. Words ending in *-tion* take the stress on the syllable just before the ending.

### Solution

oc-cu-PA-tion has the stress on the third syllable (before *-tion*). PRES-i-dent is stressed on the first, de-VEL-op-ment on the second, and com-PU-ter on the second. **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: Which syllable of the word *scientific* carries the main stress?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Words ending in *-ic* are stressed on the syllable immediately before *-ic*.

### Solution

*Scientific* ends in *-ic*, so the stress falls on the syllable just before it: sci-en-TIF-ic. **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: The word *increase* is stressed on the first syllable as a noun (INcrease) and on the second as a verb (inCREASE). In which sentence is *increase* stressed on the **first** syllable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Decide first whether the word is a noun or a verb in the sentence. Noun = first syllable, verb = second syllable.

### Solution

In (a), (b) and (c), *increase* follows *will*, *to* or a subject and is a verb: inCREASE. In (d), *an increase* is a noun: INcrease. **Answer: d.**

choix.texte: Farmers expect an increase in the price of cocoa.

enonce_markdown: Three of the words below are stressed on the same syllable. Which word is stressed on a **different** syllable from the other three?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare the stress pattern of every word before deciding; do not stop at the first one that seems right.

### Solution

MAN-go is stressed on the first syllable. ba-NA-na, to-MA-to and po-TA-to are all stressed on the second. **Answer: a.**
